title: GeoRobotix Connected Systems customer commissioning

task.name: Commission a complete Connected Systems observation window for the selected customer
task.purpose: Give a civil or environmental customer a repeatable operator workflow from the agreed Connected Systems source through complete original observations, reviewed native editions, useful queries and comparisons, and an independently received installation that can continue the same work.
task.request: Select one actual civil or environmental JSON observation endpoint, its declared result schema, permitted systems/datastreams and a bounded observation window. Record the source-use and retention authority, receiving environment, responsible technical and acceptance owners, and the useful queries to demonstrate. Retain the actual connection, discovery/schema documents, full observation pages, original identifiers and request/response history. Follow the provider's complete next chain for the selected window; retain limits, duplicate IDs, quality flags, missing values, units and provider errors. Review the supported result fields, types, key/repeated-ID policy and coverage policy before building the original SF30 edition. Query every selected row through the native cursor, compare agreed editions, and retain source, mapping and snapshot identities. Operate the complete Discovery, Sources, Mapping, Editions, Receive and Activity interface, including original-request recovery. Export the complete source/mapping/edition packet and native CSV/configuration/lineage; independently import, query, re-export and reopen the same edition in the named receiving installation. Supply editable configuration/source, applicable dependency notices and an operator walkthrough. Preserve the original Workshare's 72-hour, twelve-active-business-day commissioning scope and its separate proposed fee and acceptance phases. Customer-selected observations and the publisher's illustrative reference remain distinct source editions.
task.completeOutput: One agreed customer integration with a configured source and explicit observation window; all original pages and the declared schema; reviewed mappings and complete native editions; useful query/comparison results; visible provider and coverage findings; same-operation continuation; a complete source/edition receiving packet; native data.csv, dataset.json and source lineage; editable source/configuration and notices; and an independent receiving installation that reopens and continues the original work. The original Installation retains the actual acceptance observations and outstanding customer decisions.
task.repeatTrigger: A deliberately selected later observation window, actual source/schema change, reviewed mapping correction or customer-authorized next edition creates another attributable edition. An interrupted acquisition or download resumes the retained original operation and byte identity. Opening additional source pages within one selected window is source consumption, not an additional customer task or purchase.
task.pricedUnit: One complete agreed observation-window edition and its useful customer query/report output, with full source coverage and independent receiving. Any recurring data-service price, currency/network, atomic amount, recipient, task count and spending authority come from separately selected original merchant/customer terms. The proposed USD 9,600 engineering workshare pays for commissioning and is not a dataset offer or atomic service price.

source.reference: Select the customer's actual endpoint, permitted systems/datastreams, observation bounds and declared schema in the original case. Retain exact URLs and ordered query parameters, source timestamps and original response bytes/hashes. The committed OGC room-temperature example is a separate illustrative single-resource reference.
source.mode: Read-only Connected Systems discovery, schema and observation GETs through the existing connection/query/acquisition record. Collection acquisition follows original next links within the declared limits. An explicit single-observation resource remains a one-resource scope. A static schema URL uses the explicit exact policy; ordinary live schema requests retain the default format-parameter behavior. Closed source packets can be received without reacquiring the provider.
source.population: One customer-approved civil or environmental JSON endpoint and the agreed systems/datastreams and observation window. Retain every selected original record, including repeated IDs, source-level missing/quality values and records needing mapping review. Record returned counts, all pages, exhaustion/next-link state and every configured bound. A page or row cap is not complete source history. A single-resource reference proves only its declared one-resource scope.
source.meaning: Keep original observation id, datastream@id, resultTime and inline result structure, plus source-described time/reference frames, units, quality and external-result links. Original JSON number spellings remain available in the full response and original-observation cell. Review native types, keys, repeated-ID handling and explicit coverage policy against the declared schema. Preserve source inconsistencies as findings. The maintained engine does not infer quality thresholds, interpolate observations, convert physical units automatically or decode linked binary/video results.
source.changePolicy: Retain immutable original responses, queries, mappings, native snapshots and prior exports. A deliberate query or schema/mapping change creates a linked new edition; compare its actual rows and source metadata with the selected prior edition. A failed or ambiguous request remains in its original operation for reconciliation. Record customer withdrawal and retention changes through the existing source/Installation controls while preserving the authorized history and original commercial change decision.

receiving.application: The maintained Connected Systems CLI/operator, typed MCP client and source-owned Applications/merchant integration, backed by the original SF30 XML/native dataset engine. Use the exact selected connected-systems distribution and its runtime profile, then the original delivery/installed-receive.mjs or customer-specific native/browser receiving command. Keep the Grant Operations Installation preparer/receiver as the original programme and commercial record.
receiving.acceptanceRule: The agreed selected observation window reaches its declared end; full page/row counts, source duplicates, missing values and quality flags can be reconciled. The operator demonstrates the agreed queries and edition comparison on the original snapshots. A designated independent recipient imports the complete source/mapping/edition, queries the full native cursor, verifies exact exported bytes and reopens the same state. Acquisition and interrupted-save/download continuation retain the original identities. Editable source/configuration, notices and the operator guide are delivered; one consolidated review and in-scope defect correction complete the original Workshare. Record each actual result in the original Installation. A built archive, a publisher example or prepared merchant terms alone do not complete customer commissioning.
receiving.changeAndWithdraw: GeoRobotix retains its platform and customer relationship; the named customer technical and acceptance owners select source, scope and receiving changes. Continue the same original Installation and commercial case through their current draft/review/return operations. Additional source families, binary/video decoding, new outputs or an expanded window/retention commitment follow the Workshare's agreed price and schedule change process.
receiving.recovery: Read the saved query/acquisition/operation before continuing. Preserve failed provider documents and exact response bodies; explicit schema URL or coverage-policy corrections create linked inputs rather than rewriting the failed record. Reuse matching completed native/installed results and their verified complete files. Resume incomplete work in the retained original workspace and export cache. The browser uses the original closed native workspace and distinct receiver, then drains its servers/engine before closing. On runtime installation failure, retain the original installation/profile, state, lock and log; inspect the same graph before using the maintained resume or validated adoption route.
receiving.maintenance: Name the commissioning payer, implementation owner, GeoRobotix technical owner, accepting operator and support owner in the existing case. Customer provides source/access and rights/retention decisions, receiving environment and approximately three to five hours of review participation. Start follows agreed access/selection/receiver and commencement payment; customer/provider waits are separate from active delivery days. Supply complete editable source/configuration and upstream notices, retain credentials in the existing private configuration, and assign hosting/provider charges separately. Ongoing support, service subscriptions and production payment terms require their actual selected agreement.

steps.title: Day 1: receive the source contract and commissioning owners — 6 hours
steps.result: Inspect the actual endpoint and response/schema pair; agree systems/datastreams, selected window, bounds, source-use/retention authority and useful acceptance queries. Name payer, technical/acceptance/support owners and the receiving environment. Retain the original commercial case and its commencement conditions.

steps.title: Days 2–4: retain the complete selected acquisition — 18 hours
steps.result: Configure the original connection and query, acquire the full selected pages and preserve every raw response. Operate original-request continuation, restart and provider-error handling. Retain exhaustion, next links, limits, actual counts and the agreed retention/source configuration.

steps.title: Days 5–6: review mappings and build the first edition — 12 hours
steps.result: Inspect all supported source fields, result schema, time, units and quality metadata. Review native types/keys/repeated-ID and coverage policy. Save the complete mapping and build the original native edition, preserving original observation values and source inconsistencies.

steps.title: Day 7: demonstrate queries and edition comparison — 6 hours
steps.result: Run the agreed useful queries through complete native cursor traversal. Compare the actual selected editions with original source, mapping and snapshot identities; retain full differences and missing/duplicate/quality accounting.

steps.title: Days 8–9: operate the entire customer interface — 12 hours
steps.result: Complete Discovery through source acquisition, schema review, mapping, edition build, query/comparison, export and Receive. Review all eight retained record collections through complete view-pinned paging. Recover the same interrupted request/save/download and demonstrate deliberate next-edition selection.

steps.title: Day 10: independently install and receive the complete product — 6 hours
steps.result: Use the maintained selected archive/runtime and original receiving helper. Import the complete project in a distinct recipient, verify source/plan/snapshot and all output bytes, query every row, re-export and cold reopen. Retain any actual runtime/browser findings without marking unfinished acceptance complete.

steps.title: Day 11: consolidate review and deliver editable implementation — 6 hours
steps.result: Resolve the single consolidated in-scope review, deliver full selected source/configuration, applicable notices, source and retention instructions, and the operator guide. Keep the customer programme's complete workshare, inputs and original receiving history together.

steps.title: Day 12: complete the walkthrough and original Installation handover — 6 hours
steps.result: Walk the accepting operator through agreed source selection, useful queries/comparison, original-operation continuation and independent receiving. Save actual acceptance results and any remaining decisions in the same Installation and commercial case; export, independently receive and reopen that complete operating case.

inputs: The original complete GeoRobotix Workshare and matching native receiving packet, preserving proposed USD 9,600, USD 4,800 commencement/USD 4,800 acceptance, 72 engineering hours, twelve active business days, all original phases and start/review/change conditions.
The named commissioning payer, implementation owner, GeoRobotix/customer technical owner, accepting operator and support owner; actual contact and relationship state remain with the original sender.

One actual civil or environmental JSON endpoint, permitted systems/datastreams, declared result schema, original access method, approved observation window/bounds, source-use authority and retention policy.
Complete original provider responses/acquisition history and the customer's agreed useful queries; raw units/quality/time/source inconsistencies remain available for review.
Reviewed native mapping, coverage/repeated-ID policies, first and comparison edition identities, full native results and exact project/dataset exports.

The original connected-systems selected source archive and sourceCommit, runtime profile/lock and actual receiving environment; supplied public reference project/result are identified separately from customer observations.

The completed native/CLI/operator/MCP and independent receiver results for the selected customer, including actual original-request recovery and cold reopen; any unfinished stage remains explicitly open.
Original Operations case/plan/source IDs and the same commercial Workshare binding; any merchant/buyer deployments and recurring payment terms only when actually selected.
Complete editable source/configuration, upstream notices, operator/receiving guides, one consolidated review and agreed support/change boundaries. Provider/hosting charges are assigned separately.
